newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia files charges against Red Terror suspects.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia files charges against Red Terror suspects.

text.p: Ethiopia said on Wednesday it has charged over 1,200 people suspected of involvement in the Red Terror campaign during the 14-year Marxist rule of ousted dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam.
The state-run Ethiopia News Agency (ENA) reported that the charges were filed by the office of the registrar of the Federal High Court in the capital, Addis Ababa.
The Red Terror was a campaign against rival Marxist groups and those opposed to Mengistu's military rule.
An estimated one million people died of starvation during Mengistu's brutal rule. Hundreds of thousands were killed in civil war and political violence.
The trial of 71 former Ethiopian Marxist officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity is in progress in the capital Addis Ababa.
Only 46 of the officials appeared in court. The others including Mengistu, who lives in exile in Zimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.
All 46 have pleaded not guilty to the charges. They face the death penalty if found guilty.
The former officials are members of the Dergue, the miltiary junta led by Mengistu which ruled Ethiopia after ousting Emperor Haile Selassie whom, they later killed.

"The office of the registrar of the Federal High Court in Addis Ababa said it has received charges filed by the special prosecutor against 1,218 alleged perpetrators of the notorious Red Terror," the agency said.
"The office of the registrar has begun examining charges and will refer them to pertinent benches," it added.

Eyewitnesses said during the 1977-78 Red Terror campaign, Mengistu's hit-men hunted down thousands of students from rival Marxist groups and other opposition groups throughout the Horn of Africa nation and gunned them down in broad daylight.
Their bodies were thrown on road sides and public squares as warning to others, they added.
Some estimates put those butchered during the 1977-78 campaign in the capital Addis Ababa alone close to 26,000.
Residents remember that grieving parents in the capital who went to mortuaries to claim the bodies of their loved ones were charged for the cost of bullets used to kill them.
